Zwift goes big and early with up to 27% off for Black Friday – Grab your Zwift Cyber Week deal now

News
By Paul Brett

Zwift has dropped its Black Friday deals a week early, and highlights include $300 off the Zwift Ride V2 bundle equipped with the Kickr Core 2 and the Cog and Click, but you'll have to be quick to grab these limited-time deals

The year's biggest shopping weekend is now just one week away, with Black Friday officially running from November 27 through Cyber Monday on November 30.

However, you don't have to wait until actual Black Friday to score some huge savings, because the cycling deals are already dropping, led by some of the most eagerly awaited offers of the year from Zwift.

Zwift has gone big and early with the launch of Zwift Cyber Week, which runs from November 20 to November 30.

Shop the Zwift Cyber Week deals and save up to 27%.

Gearing up or upgrading your indoor cycling setup can be an expensive business, and I know of several people who have been holding back, waiting for the Zwift Black Friday deals.

The standout discount is on what is regarded as the ultimate Zwift set-up: the Zwift Ride V2 bundle, with $300, £200, or €200 off, depending on your location.

The Zwift Ride bundle comes with everything you need for indoor riding season, including the updated Ride V2 smart frame, the Kickr Core 2 and the Cog and Click virtual shifting and gearing system.

The Zwift Ride V2 is rated as one of the best smart bikes on the market. It builds on the original Ride by adding multi-length cranks, expanded saddle adjustability, and a wider-diameter handlebar. It makes dialling in your perfect fit a breeze, with a one-tool system for simple adjustment, so you can get riding faster.

New users will also be entitled to a 14-day free trial of Zwift Plus, which is a higher-tier cycling subscription from Zwift that adds Zwift Coach (adaptive training plans) and Zwift Video (4K real-world video routes).

If you want to bring your outdoor bike inside on a budget, the Wahoo Kickr Core 2 with the Zwift Cog and Click system is one of the best smart trainer packages on the market.

Replacing standard rear cogs with Zwift’s universal Cog delivers ultra-quiet virtual shifting managed directly from your handlebars, alongside easy in-game navigation. Nearly any 8- to 13-speed bike fits out of the box. Performance remains top-tier: it handles up to 1,800 watts, simulates gradients up to 16%, and maintains ±2% power accuracy, with onboard Wi-Fi ensuring drop-free connectivity.

With 27% off in the US and EU, and 20% off for UK shoppers, it's a direct saving of $150, €150, or £100 and great value for those who choose to ride their outdoor bike for winter indoor riding.

Purchasers of the Wahoo Kickr Core 2 during Zwift Cyber Week will also receive a free month of Zwift Plus (worth $29.99, £26.99, €29.99).

The Zwift Cog is paired with Zwift Click controllers and enables silent, virtual shifting. It gives users full control of gearing, but also in-game control of all of Zwift. Meaning you can navigate with ease to queue your next ride or workout, use PowerUps, give a Ride On, and more without ever taking your hands off the bars.

If a Zwift Cyber Week deal isn't on your Black Friday radar, then the Cyclingnews Black Friday 2026 Cycling Deals hub is live and has a load of the best early deals, selected by our deal-hunting experts.

With cycling tech always a Black Friday highlight, there are plenty of offerings on the best bike computers, smartwatches, and bike lights.

Deals writer

Paul Brett is a deals writer for Cyclingnews and has been cycling for as long as he can remember, initially catching the mountain biking bug in the 1990s, he raced mountain bikes for over a decade before injury cut short a glittering career. An award-winning photographer, when not riding a bike, he can be found at the side of a road world championship or a cyclocross track shooting the action. Paul was the founder, editor and writer of Proper Cycling magazine, and he's travelled the world interviewing some of the top personalities in cycling and writing about some of the biggest cycling brands.
